mars_target: High-latitude Martian ground ice in vapor exchange with the atmosphere
claim: University Valley has air temperatures that stay below freezing, no bulk liquid water, and dry permafrost above ice-cemented ground that exchanges vapor with the atmosphere.
caveat: A climate layer can screen for few days above freezing. It cannot see the ice table.

mars_target: Local controls on Martian ground-ice depth
claim: Ice-cemented ground is at the surface at the valley head and deeper than 70 cm at the mouth. A weather station about a third of the way down the valley recorded 42 cm.
caveat: Depth was measured in pits and boreholes. Slope and snow recurrence are partial explanations, not a remote measurement of depth.

mars_target: Snow or frost control on Martian ground-ice stability
claim: Modeled thin seasonal snow deposits can strongly slow, and in the model can stop, ablation of the University Valley ice table.
caveat: Satellite snow cover is hundreds of meters across. The stabilizing deposits in the model are thin and local.

mars_target: Salt effects on high-latitude ground ice, including perchlorate
claim: Without snow, NaCl, CaCl2, and perchlorate in the surface soil slightly increase ice-table recession by holding vapor. Hygroscopic salts can also form near-surface pore ice.
caveat: EMIT does not cover this latitude. Salt profiles stay reference-only.

mars_target: Phoenix landing site, Martian northern plains
claim: Compared with lower Taylor Valley, University Valley soils keep salts, clay-sized material, and biomass near the surface, consistent with little downward water transport. The Phoenix site is interpreted as even more arid.
caveat: The comparison uses soil pits, chemistry, and biomass counts. It is not a satellite classification.

process_name: Aqueous salt transport and higher biomass
mars_target: A wetter contrast to the Phoenix soils, not the Phoenix analog itself
claim: Lower Taylor Valley soils show clay-sized particle distributions and less abundant soluble salts that suggest water transport, plus higher microbial biomass and aqueous alteration of mica.
caveat: Summer warmth and open water can be screened remotely. The soil-transport claim cannot.

process_name: Massive ground ice under sublimation till
mars_target: Debris-covered massive ice, distinct from pore ice
claim: At the central Beacon Valley polygon, massive ground ice with about 10 wt% debris lies 30-50 cm below the surface, under 0.30 m of sublimation residue.
caveat: The ice was drilled and instrumented. Surface roughness does not identify it.

process_name: Polygons do not identify ice type
mars_target: Patterned ground over Martian ground ice
claim: Contraction polygons overlie massive ice in central Beacon Valley and also occur where University Valley has ice-cemented ground rather than massive ice. Polygon form alone does not identify the ice.
caveat: Polygons can be mapped. The subsurface ice type still requires a pit, a drill, or a geophysical survey.

process_name: Age of Beacon Valley massive ice
mars_target: How long debris-covered ice can persist
claim: Ash in the overlying till was interpreted as evidence that the ice has persisted since at least 8.1 Ma. Vapor-diffusion calculations make that survival difficult unless humidity and temperature strongly slow the loss. A snow-aware model gives about 0.09 mm/yr over 200 ka and is used to argue the ice is older than 1 Ma. Liu et al. 2018 say the ice has been sublimating for at least 200 ka, which is a minimum duration of loss, not a maximum age.
caveat: Do not treat 200 ka as the age of the ice, and do not treat 8.1 Ma as settled.

mars_target: Recharge of shallow ground ice
claim: At about 450 m elevation the ice cement is 0.22 m down. Modeled sublimation is about 0.22 mm/yr, too fast to leave ice that shallow after 10 ka unless summer snow and snowmelt recharge the soil.
caveat: This is a lower, seasonally warmer site than University Valley. Snow cover here is not the same stability regime.

mars_target: Recurring slope lineae and ancient chloride deposits
claim: Don Juan Pond is fed by CaCl2-rich brines moving on the permafrost table and by small melt inputs. Deliquescence concentrates moisture in saline soils. Deep groundwater discharge was not observed in the imaged season.
caveat: Dark water tracks can be imaged. Brine chemistry cannot be read from NDVI or a DEM.

mars_target: Not a Mars landing-site analog in the opened 2009 paper
claim: Blood Falls releases an anoxic, ferrous, sulfate-rich brine from beneath Taylor Glacier. A microbial sulfur cycle uses Fe(III) as the electron acceptor. The paper compares this isolated metabolism with organic-starved oceans.
caveat: Stored so the brine is not merged with the University Valley dry-permafrost claim. Not a search seed.

process_name: Basaltic sand sheet as a Stimson analog
mars_target: Stimson formation, Gale crater
claim: The Askja sand sheet is a cold-climate basaltic eolian deposit with millimeter-scale lamination and cross-bedding. Sara et al. compare that structure, and the sand's MgO and Fe2O3, with the Stimson sandstone.
caveat: Dune and sand-sheet morphology can be screened. Grain mineralogy and lamination cannot.

mars_target: Spatial variation inside one eolian deposit
claim: The sheet is centimeters to about 10 m thick and about 240 km2. The southwest is deflationary basaltic sand, the center is inflating sand with ripples and relict lava, and the northeast traps pumice-rich sand in depressions.
caveat: The facies boundaries in this catalog are not georeferenced.

process_name: Northeast pumice excluded from the Stimson comparison
mars_target: Stimson formation, Gale crater
claim: The northeast sand is mostly 1875 Askja pumice plus local basalt. Sara et al. did not treat it as part of the basaltic Stimson comparison because the chemistry differs.
caveat: A visual match to the rest of the sheet would be the wrong seed.

mars_target: Martian basaltic sand and the unaltered Stimson
claim: Surface sand is basalt fragments, volcanic glass, olivine, pyroxene, and plagioclase. Reported bulk ranges are about 48-52 wt% SiO2, 5-8 wt% MgO, and 13-15 wt% Fe2O3.
caveat: Askja is outside the EMIT latitude window. Do not impute these oxide values from a mineral map.

process_name: Holuhraun lava on the sand sheet
mars_target: Not the Stimson analog
claim: The 2014-2015 Holuhraun lava was emplaced on the southeastern sand sheet and may have added ash and changed the local MgO trend.
caveat: The flow can be mapped. It is a disturbance of the eolian deposit.

mars_target: None. Historical lunar-crew training.
claim: Apollo crews used Askja for geology training. That history does not define a transferable physical feature.
caveat: Gazetteer source. Not a geological process.

process_name: Young basalt as an alteration-state analog
mars_target: Older Martian basalt with limited aqueous alteration
claim: The studied north-flank flows are about 200 years old and sparsely vegetated. Bleacher et al. use that youth because aqueous alteration is faster on Earth than on Mars, so young Hawaiian basalt can resemble the alteration state of much older Martian basalt.
caveat: Barren basalt can be screened. Flow age has to come from a geologic map, not from NDVI.

process_name: Lava tubes, skylights, and surface detection
mars_target: Martian lava tubes and skylights
claim: Two tube segments on the north flank were entered through skylights. Surface magnetics and GPR detected void space, and interior lidar mapped the tube. Surface geophysics did not by itself recover the tube dimensions.
caveat: Orbital roughness is not a tube map. The tube coordinates were not published in the abstract.

process_name: Secondary salts in young lava tubes
mars_target: Secondary minerals and possible biosignatures in Martian lava tubes
claim: Interior coatings include Na sulfates, calcite, gypsum, and monohydrocalcite. The site is high enough to limit sea-salt input, so the salts are attributed to basalt and volcanic aerosol. Preliminary sequencing found Proteobacteria and Actinobacteria.
caveat: These minerals were measured inside the tube. A surface mineral map does not sample them.

mars_target: MER APXS weathering indices and orbital clay or hydrated-silica detections
claim: Within 6 km of HI-SEAS, the top 2-3 cm of pahoehoe older than about 400 years contains Fe/Mg-smectite, hydrated silica, Al-silicates, Al-hydroxide, and palagonite. Weathering indices match a low degree of alteration in an arid to semi-arid, cool to moderate setting, similar to MER APXS results.
caveat: Conference abstract, not a journal paper. EMIT may detect related surface minerals here and cannot see the top 2-3 cm depth profile. This is not a CheMin comparison.

mars_target: None as a ground feature
claim: HI-SEAS is an isolation habitat used for crew and operations studies. Isolation, crew selection, and communications delay are not properties of the lava.
caveat: The surrounding lava is cataloged separately.

mars_target: Impact-generated hydrothermal systems
claim: Four settings are distinguished: vugs and veins in crater-fill melt breccia, cementation in the central uplift, veining at the uplift margin, and pipes or gossans on rim faults. Early temperatures were at least about 200 C and later precipitation continued below about 100 C. Minerals include quartz, calcite, marcasite, celestite, barite, and fluorite.
caveat: The settings are structural and mineralogical. Distance to the crater is only a locator, not evidence of alteration.

process_name: Vugs and veins in crater-fill melt breccia
mars_target: Impact-generated hydrothermal systems
claim: Hydrothermal vugs and veins in the crater-fill melt breccia become more intense toward the base of the unit.
caveat: No sample coordinate was printed in the opened abstract.

mars_target: Impact-generated hydrothermal systems
claim: Brecciated lithologies in the central uplift were cemented, with quartz mineralization in two temperature episodes.
caveat: No sample coordinate was printed in the opened abstract.

mars_target: Impact-generated hydrothermal systems
claim: The faulted outer margin of the central uplift has intense calcite veining from about 150 C down to below about 60 C.
caveat: No sample coordinate was printed in the opened abstract.

mars_target: Impact-generated hydrothermal systems
claim: Hydrothermal pipes or gossans, with calcite, quartz, marcasite, and pyrite, follow fault surfaces around the crater rim.
caveat: No pipe coordinate was printed in the opened abstract. Impact distance does not identify a pipe.

mars_target: Impact process analog, not a basalt lithology analog
claim: The target is about 1880 m of Paleozoic carbonate-dominated sediment, with evaporites, over crystalline basement. The crater-fill melt groundmass includes calcite, silicate glass, and anhydrite.
caveat: GLiM can keep this carbonate terrain from matching Hawaiian or Askja basalt. It cannot map the melt breccia.

mars_target: Duration of the hydrothermal and lake record
claim: Sherlock et al. report an Ar/Ar age of about 39 Ma from shocked basement clasts. Young et al. report a zircon (U-Th)/He age of 23.5 ± 2.0 Ma. Osinski et al. 2005a use the about 39 Ma age. The Haughton-Mars Project page says the crater formed about 23 million years ago and is 20 km across, which also differs from the about 23 km apparent and about 16 km rim diameters in Osinski et al. 2005a.
caveat: Do not collapse the age to one number. The website diameter is not the mapped apparent diameter.

mars_target: Polar-desert permafrost with a seasonal active layer
claim: Haughton soils are carbonate-rich and have abundant ice-wedge polygons. The summer active layer is about 50-70 cm. Glass and Seitz cite continuous permafrost of roughly 600 m to a paper that was not opened here.
caveat: This active layer means seasonal thaw, unlike University Valley's no-thaw dry permafrost. The 600 m thickness is not independently checked.

process_name: Drill testing in icy fallback breccia
mars_target: Icy subsurface sampling, including Icebreaker-type drills
claim: Drill Hill is a 150 m thick fallback-breccia deposit with intermittent clear ice and periglacial structure. Several planetary drill prototypes were tested there.
caveat: The test record is operational. The icy breccia is the physical analog, and it is not the same material as Antarctic dry permafrost.

mars_target: Intra-crater lake deposits
claim: After erosion of the crater-fill impactites, the Haughton Formation lake sediments were deposited in the crater. They are a later sedimentary record, not the hydrothermal mineral assemblage.
caveat: The unit is mapped in the papers. It is not separated by a global lithology class.

mars_target: Endolithic habitats in impact-processed rock
claim: The opened FMARS manuscript describes simulated-EVA sampling of shocked rock for microbiology and points to a companion manuscript, then in press, on impact-induced endolithic habitats. That companion paper was not opened.
caveat: This catalog supports the sampling context, not an unopened habitat result. The present crater is not an active warm hydrothermal oasis.

process_name: Glacial troughs as a canyon hypothesis
mars_target: Martian canyon tributaries, as a project hypothesis
claim: The Haughton-Mars Project page compares Devon Island glacial troughs, including Astronaut Canyon, with a tributary of Ius Chasma on the basis of shape, scale, and geologic setting.
caveat: Valley shape can be measured. The glacial origin of the Martian canyons is not established by this comparison, so the site is not a search seed.
